summary: Brazil's foreign ministry visa table gives, for visit visas, an exemption for up to 90 days to nationals of countries such as the United Kingdom, Germany, Italy, Japan, Mexico and Argentina, an exemption for up to 30 days to China, and a visa requirement for the United States, Canada, Australia and India. The Consulate-General of Brazil in Miami says citizens of Australia, Canada and the United States can apply for an electronic visitor visa through brazil.vfsevisa.com (fee US$ 80.90), and that a regular visitor visa can be obtained in person at the consulate.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Brazil?
faq.answer: Yes. Brazil's foreign ministry visa table lists a visa requirement for the United States, and the Consulate-General of Brazil in Miami says US citizens can apply for the electronic visitor visa through brazil.vfsevisa.com, with an e-visa fee of US$ 80.90. The eVisa portal says the eVisa is valid for 5 or 10 years on multiple entries, that once in Brazil you are authorised to stay up to 90 days per year, and that to extend beyond 90 days you should contact the Federal Police.

faq.question: Which nationalities can visit Brazil without a visa?
faq.answer: Brazil's foreign ministry visa table gives a visa exemption for up to 90 days, for visit purposes, to nationals of countries including the United Kingdom, Germany, Italy, Switzerland, Japan, South Korea, Turkey, South Africa, Mexico, Argentina, Chile, Colombia and Peru. It lists a visa requirement for the United States, Canada, Australia, India and Nigeria; the Consulate-General in Miami says citizens of Australia, Canada and the United States can use the electronic visitor visa.

faq.question: How do I apply for the Brazilian eVisa?
faq.answer: The Consulate-General of Brazil in Miami says all e-Visa requests must be made through brazil.vfsevisa.com, with an e-visa fee of US$ 80.90. The portal asks for a recent photograph and a colour copy of the passport bio page, and says processing takes up to 10 business days once your verified application is submitted.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Brazil?
faq.answer: No, it is not an entry requirement: Brazil's Ministry of Health says there is no obligation to show proof of vaccination to enter the country. It indicates the yellow fever vaccine for travellers going to the areas where vaccination is recommended, at least 10 days before travel, and says the International Certificate of Vaccination is important when the destination country or a country of transit requires it.

faq.question: Can I extend my 90-day stay in Brazil?
faq.answer: Under Decree No. 9199 of 2017 (art. 20), a visit visa allows a stay of up to 90 days, extendable by the Federal Police by up to 90 days, provided the maximum stay does not exceed 180 days in each migratory year. The extension may only be granted to nationals of countries that ensure reciprocal treatment for Brazilians, and must be requested before the original stay expires. Article 23 says the same rule may be applied to nationals of visa-exempt countries. The foreign ministry's visa table marks some nationalities, for example Germany and Italy, with a maximum stay of 90 days every 180 days.
